This summer, Apple raised product prices significantly due to an ongoing global memory crisis. The iPad Air jumped from $599 to $749, the MacBook Pro with the M5 chip rose from $1,699 to $1,999, and the Apple TV climbed from $129 to $199. These are just a few examples, but the point is that these increases are substantial.

This situation naturally raises the question — will Apple make major improvements to its products to make them more appealing to consumers at the new price points?

Of course, some Apple products are getting major updates soon, such as the MacBook Pro and iPad mini. But for products that aren't receiving significant updates anytime soon, I struggle to see how Apple can successfully sell yesterday's technology at much higher prices and make consumers feel they're getting their money's worth — especially compared with current second-hand market prices.

If just a few months ago you could buy an M4 iPad Air for $599 (or even as low as $499), why would you want to pay $749 for the same device now? This logic applies even more clearly to higher-priced products.

Some Apple products haven't changed much in a long time. The iPad Air has used the same design and feature set since 2020, with only chip upgrades and the addition of Apple Pencil Pro support. The entry-level iPad has remained largely unchanged since 2022, and the iMac since 2021.

Do these products need a redesign? Not necessarily. But I think Apple could do something at the current price points to make them more attractive. For example, the iMac could get a mini-LED display, the iPad Air could be upgraded to a 120Hz refresh rate, and the entry-level iPad could get a fully laminated display.

Compared with price increases, these upgrades would be relatively low-cost, but they should help consumers feel they're getting better value at the new price points. On the other hand, Apple might also downgrade some products to offset the price increases — for example, the iPhone could once again offer a 128GB storage option.

What are your thoughts on Apple's product lineup after the price increases? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
